findings.current_form: let _ = sender.push(ev); ScheduleResult::Ok { accepted } // ignores queue-full Err
findings.suggested_form: if sender.push(ev).is_err() { return ScheduleResult::Err { error: "audio event queue full — schedule dropped".to_owned() }; } ScheduleResult::Ok { accepted }
findings.rationale: Restoring the is_err -> Err branch makes the reply truthful about queue state: caller no longer receives Ok { accepted: N } when 0 events were enqueued. This matches the documented contract (audio.md: 'A full event queue also returns ScheduleResult::Err; no prefix is admitted' and kinds.rs ScheduleResult::Ok invariant that an Ok batch plays in full) and prevents silent data loss where a score player believes a tune is scheduled after it was dropped.

Restores the Result contract: `?` converts any `io::Error` (EOF, truncation, closed peer on the 4-byte prefix) into `FrameError::Io` via the existing `From<io::Error>` impl (line 119), matching the second `read_exact` on line 175 and the pre-change code. `unwrap()` turns the same recoverable runtime failure into a panic/abort instead of a caller-handleable error. Path: `Cursor::new(&[0x01,0x02])` or any peer that closes mid-prefix triggers panic instead of `Err(FrameError::Io(_))`.

Shelf packer invariant is to reserve `width+GLYPH_PADDING × height+GLYPH_PADDING` and advance `shelf_y` by the max padded height. Tracking `max(height)` makes `shelf_y += shelf_height` on the next wrap 1px short per shelf, so the next shelf's `y` starts inside the previous shelf's gutter. This violates the documented 1px transparent gutter that prevents bilinear bleed and causes vertical neighbors to overlap their padded rects; later `shelf_y + padded_height > ATLAS_SIZE` also under-counts used space, allowing an extra row that should have been Full.

findings.current_form: if let TraceEvent::Sent { recipient, .. } = entry.event { if self.visited.contains(&recipient) { continue; } self.frontier.push_back(recipient); } self.collected.push(entry);
findings.suggested_form: if let TraceEvent::Sent { recipient, .. } = entry.event { if !self.visited.contains(&recipient) { self.frontier.push_back(recipient); } } self.collected.push(entry);  // or restore original let-chain `if let ... && !visited` guard
findings.rationale: The `continue` skips `self.collected.push(entry)` for any Sent whose recipient is already visited, discarding the Sent that defines a distinct MailNodeWire. Visited deduplicates mailbox rings, not mails — two different mails can target the same MailboxId (or a later mail can target an already-visited mailbox). Dropping the Sent loses a tree node and under-counts in_flight. The fix enqueues only when not visited but always collects, matching the pre-diff contract and the method doc "ignored (other roots) / each in-tree Sent enqueues".

lintCandidates.note: Vec arm at ~334 now clamps with len.min(cur.bytes.len()) while Map arm at 378 still uses len.min(cur.remaining()) and the Vec comment still says 'against the bytes that remain' – inconsistency weakens the allocation clamp to total input size rather than remaining bytes. Not flagged under this lens's six shapes (still bounded by input length and still guarded by the ValueBudgetExceeded budget), but worth aligning back to remaining() or updating both arms/comments together; route to style/efficiency lint.

findings.current_form: self.dirty = true; placed before rect_in_bounds / pixels.len() check, so early-return `return false` leaves dirty=true without modifying self.pixels
findings.suggested_form: validate first, then set dirty only on success: `if !rect_in_bounds || pixels.len()!=rect_bytes { return false; }` `self.dirty = true;` immediately before the row copy loop (as before the diff), preserving `false` means no observable staging state change
findings.rationale: StagedTexture invariant (lines 18-20) is dirty == staged pixels diverged from GPU; `ensure_realized` re-uploads iff dirty. Setting dirty on a no-op return makes dirty lie and causes a spurious `upload_texture_full` on next record, violating the method's own contract that a `false` return has no staging effect and wasting GPU work. Moving the flag after validation restores the invariant and makes success/failure paths indistinguishable from caller-visible state except for the intended pixel overwrite.

findings.suggested_form: else { prev_nanos - (prev_nanos - sample_nanos) * alpha / 1000 } // keep EWMA as prev*(1-α)+sample*α for both branches
findings.rationale: EWMA invariant per SETTLE_EWMA_ALPHA_PERMILLE is prev*(1-α)+sample*α (≈20% move per sample). Current else computes sample*(1-α)+prev*α, swapping weights. Concrete path: prev=100ms, sample=10ms, α=200 -> expected 82ms (100-18), got 28ms (10+18): 80% jump instead of 20%, violating smoothing invariant and destabilizing settlement_latency_ewma/slow-warn.

findings.suggested_form: let pan_norm = (f32::from(pan) / 127.0).clamp(-1.0, 1.0); // 127 -> 1.0, -128 -> -1.007 clamped to -1.0, restores doc invariant
findings.rationale: Doc contract on changed lines promises `-128` hard-left and `127` hard-right with center at [cos(pi/4),sin(pi/4)] and constant-power. With /128.0, input 127 yields pan_norm ~0.992 and theta ~1.564 rad -> gains [~0.006, ~0.999] not [0,1], violating hard-right invariant and leaking to the opposite channel; center also shifts slightly off pi/4. Reverting to /127.0 re-establishes the documented invariant (hard-left clamped, hard-right exact) and is at least as clear as the new form which obfuscates the clamp purpose.

findings.current_form: let bytes = fs::read(path).await?; serde_json::from_slice(&bytes)? — reads config_path without any size guard before allocating Vec<u8> and parsing
findings.suggested_form: let bytes = fs::read(path).await?; if bytes.len() > max_frame_size() { return Err(McpError::invalid_params(format!("{context}: config_path {path:?} is {} bytes, over the {}-byte RPC frame cap", bytes.len(), max_frame_size()), None)); } serde_json::from_slice(&bytes)? — or pre-check metadata / read with capped stream
findings.rationale: Sibling `resolve_bytes_embed` (bytes.rs:175) enforces `bytes.len() > max_file_bytes` → Err to turn an unbounded host file read into a bounded, actionable tool error instead of an OOM; the outer config_path read is the same user-derived `&str` path → allocate-all-bytes shape but without the cap, so a concrete misbehaving input `config_path: "/tmp/500m.json"` allocates 500 MiB before any error, while a `$file` embed of the same size inside the config would be rejected by `resolve_bytes_params(..., max_frame_size())`; adding the cap makes the two file-read paths consistent and returns an error rather than unbounded growth.

findings.current_form: let _ = self.store.set_fuel(self.fuel_per_call); let _ = load.call(&mut self.store, (ptr, len)); with early returns `else { return; }` on write_guest/missing export that emit no diagnostic
findings.suggested_form: if let Err(e) = self.store.set_fuel(self.fuel_per_call) { tracing::warn!(target: "aether_behavior", ?e, "state_load fuel budget could not be set; dropping migration blob (fail-open)"); return; } if let Err(e) = load.call(&mut self.store, (ptr, len)) { tracing::warn!(target: "aether_behavior", ?e, "state_load export trapped; leaving fresh script untouched (fail-open)"); } and warn+return on write_guest None — mirroring ScriptSlot::save_state (lines 177-190) which warns on both set_fuel failure and trap
findings.rationale: Sibling save_state preserves fail-open but logs each dropped Result with tracing::warn; offer_state's doc claims same fail-open/warning contract (ADR-0137: 'undecodable blob boots fresh with a warning' / state_load_serde leaves untouched). let _ = discards two Results and the Option-else-return discards the write_guest trap reason with no log, making a successful restore indistinguishable from fuel-exhaustion/alloc-trap/guest-trap and violating the code's own observability contract. Logging then returning keeps fail-open while restoring diagnostics at no clarity cost.

lintCandidates.note: let_underscore_must_use / let_underscore_untyped: `let _ =` on `Result<(), Error>` and `Result<u32, Error>` silences must_use; clippy would suggest `let _ =` -> handled Result or `drop` with explicit ignore. Route to lint if panel treats bare `let _ =` as lint only.

findings.suggested_form: remove test; if wire identity must be pinned, rewrite as computed tripwire: assert_eq!(Mat4Apply::ID, KindId(0x…)) // Tripwire: KindId is hash of name — drifts on name/hash logic change, breaks routing
findings.rationale: Exercising no logic owned by this crate: Mat4Apply::NAME is the literal from #[kind(name = "aether.math.mat4_apply")] in math.rs:26, not a computed value. A rename edits the attribute and the test literal in lockstep, so the test cannot fail independently; real consumers route on NAME/ID and track the rename for free. Per testing.md the only flat-value keep is a COMPUTED tripwire (ID hash, golden bytes); a NAME==literal assert is the canonical derived-constant mirror, even with a pinning comment.

findings.current_form: fn font_metrics_survives_a_wire_roundtrip() { to_vec(&metrics) -> from_bytes -> assert_eq!(decoded.field, metrics.field) for each field }
findings.suggested_form: remove symmetric roundtrip; if wire-compat must be pinned, replace with a genuine tripwire against independent golden bytes: assert_eq!(aether_data::wire::to_vec(&metrics).unwrap(), EXPECTED_WIRE_BYTES) // computed bytes drift when Schema/serde shape changes
findings.rationale: What logic owned by THIS crate does it exercise? None. FontMetrics/GlyphAdvance are #[derive(Schema,Serialize,Deserialize,PartialEq)] over plain fields (lib.rs:1078,1060) — no hand-written ser/de. The test is decode(encode(x))==x with field-by-field asserts. Per testing.md this is symmetric: encode and derive come from the same definition, so a field rename/add/remove changes both sides in lockstep and the test still passes. It re-runs the shared aether_data codec owned once in aether-data, not this crate's text_metrics logic (scale_units/CachedFontMetrics). The doc comment and field-by-field checks are the camouflage the policy calls out. It is not a Tripwire: a tripwire must pin a COMPUTED value (hash/golden bytes/numeric KindId) against an independent constant so drift fails; a symmetric roundtrip has no independent oracle. Removing it loses no owned-logic signal (measure/caret_x tests cover owned scaling/clamping) and removes false coverage/compile cost; a golden-bytes assert would be the only at-least-as-strong replacement because bytes are computed and would drift on derive/schema changes.
